A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Logicbreaks research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original learned-reasoner accuracy, attack-success experiments, token-substitution analyses, and GPT-2/Llama-2 attention measurements in Sections 3–4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds linear-probing experiments measuring proof-state recovery from GPT-2 representations, including under attack, in Section 4 and Figure 5.

M1.justification: The transformer construction, binary encoding, autoregressive inference, three theoretical attacks, and learned/GCG attack procedures remain unchanged. The new linear probes are diagnostic analyses, not modifications to the proposed reasoner or attacks.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic Horn-logic inference, Minecraft crafting at depths 1, 3, and 5, and the same 15 custom Llama-2 prompts. Probing uses restrictions of the existing Minecraft data; it adds representation analysis rather than a new domain or rule-following scenario.

E2.justification: The reported experiments retain the same theoretical attacks, learned suffixes, GCG, and manual attacks. Although v2's main text says Llama-2 was not attacked with GCG, Appendix D.4 retains the same five exploratory GCG trials as v1's Appendix C.3; comparator removal is therefore not established.

E3.justification: v2 adds a separate probing protocol: 48 logistic-regression probes across 12 layers and four proposition counts, trained on 1024 or 2048 prompts and validated on 256, using exact-state accuracy and F1. Existing training and attack protocols remain. Table 4's new last-rule-token description conflicts with the unchanged maximum-over-rule-tokens aggregation in Appendix D.3.

E4.justification: Section 4 and Figure 5 add a substantive analysis of whether binary proof states are recoverable from GPT-2 representations, varying layer and proposition count and examining adversarial-state recovery. This directly tests the theoretical abstraction's empirical relevance. Existing capacity, repetition, attention, and token-substitution analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The uncertainty values in v2's Table 1 already appear in v1's Appendix Table 6. The median-over-five-seeds accuracy figure is retained as v2 Figure 7, formerly v1 Figure 3. No new repeated-run or uncertainty-estimation practice is reported.

E6.justification: Figure 5 adds a new family of representation results: deeper layers generally support better decoding, larger proposition sets reduce recovery, and attacked representations favor the adversarial state. Existing numerical attack results remain unchanged after matching tables and figures. The stated layers of strongest GPT-2 attention suppression change from 5–7 to 6–8 without changes to the table values.

T1.justification: The MMS definitions, transformer-encoding and attack theorems, mathematical constructions, and Appendix A–B proofs are substantively unchanged. The added discussion of first-order applicability and empirical tightness does not introduce a new formal result or assumption.

C1.justification: v2's abstract and introduction explicitly claim alignment between LLM reasoning and the theoretical constructions, extending v1's emphasis on attack transfer and resemblance. The core Horn-logic framework, three attack categories, and theory-to-practice contribution remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets probing as support for binary-state modeling and existing small-model results as suggesting construction tightness. It adds a first-order limitation of maximality and explains the incompleteness criterion used for text generation. The conclusion no longer explicitly lists negation and disjunction limitations, although broader expressivity limitations remain.

D1.justification: The new probing study specifies last-token representations, 768-dimensional inputs, layer-specific linear classifiers, logistic-regression fitting, and sample counts. Existing optimizer settings, hardware, training times, data-generation instructions, and source-code/data references are retained across the reorganized appendices.

R1.justification: v2 adds Manning et al. on probing and removes the Chandra–Harel Horn-clause reference and safeguarding references concerning goal prioritization and directed representation optimization. Positioning against transformer-expressivity and BERT reasoning work remains substantially unchanged. Consolidating duplicate Jailbroken references does not remove that work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and several explanatory passages are rewritten. Section 3.1 shifts emphasis toward LLM representations, Section 4 reorganizes three result headings into five, and the experimental appendix splits into separate learned-reasoner and LLM sections. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds the three-panel probing Figure 5, moves the unchanged accuracy heatmaps from main-text Figure 3 to appendix Figure 7, and consolidates v1 Tables 1 and 6 into Table 1. Other tables are reordered and plots receive styling adjustments, while the overall visual format remains similar.

improvement.justification: The probing study provides useful new evidence connecting theoretical proof states to GPT-2 representations, strengthening an important empirical link. The gain is limited because recoverability does not establish the proposed causal reasoning mechanism. New inconsistencies about Llama-2 GCG use and attention aggregation also reduce reporting clarity, but do not outweigh the added evidence.
